author: wafflefries

13 iccanobiF

Rules:

• Normal sudoku rules apply.

• Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.

• iccanobiF lines are Fibonacci lines that read from right to left.

• Put any two numbers into the bulbs to the right of the lines.

• Add the two numbers in the bulb, and if the sum is a single digit number, place it into the consecutive cell along the line to the left of the rightmost digit.

• If the sum is a two-digit number, place the 2 digits in separate cells IN READING ORDER (left to right) in the next two consecutive cells along the line to the left of the rightmost digit.

• Two-digit numbers are always on the same row.

• Repeat the process, always adding the two leftmost digits on the line (even if the two leftmost digits are from a two-digit number).

Changes from Fibonacci 8:
• I have added a bulb to denote the starting of the line. As a setter, I think this is a good optional addition that can be purposefully left off in order to create an ambiguously directioned line.

• I have decided to change the color from lilac to gray. This was a decision that LMD member Richard chose, and I think it is a good change. I used the standard Arrow, changed the thickness to 20, changes the head size to 5, then added a 20-thick segment of Cosmetic Lines of color #aaaaaa to smooth out the end of the line.

• The name "iccanobiF Lines" is unnecessary, as the rule to always "put the 2 digit line in reading order on the same row" will apply to many variations of the line (and will throw off the familiar patterns for those that have solved the full Fibonacci series!)
